authority: NASA NSSDCA (Goddard Space Flight Center), curator D. R. Williams
title: Apollo Landing Site Coordinates
verified: Table 'Lunar Module' rows read Apollo 11 0.67416 N / 23.47314 E, Apollo 12 -3.0128 / -23.4219, Apollo 14 -3.64589 / -17.47194, Apollo 15 26.13239 / 3.63330, Apollo 16 -8.9734 / 15.5011, Apollo 17 20.1911 / 30.7723; page states planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421, from LRO images per Wagner et al., Icarus 283, 92-103 (2017).

authority: NASA NSSDCA (Goddard Space Flight Center), curator D. R. Williams
title: Table of Anthropogenic Impacts and Spacecraft on the Moon
verified: Table gives date and lat/lon (N/S, E/W and N,E-positive columns) for each object, e.g. Chang'e 4 '45.4561 S, 177.5885 E', SLIM '13.3160 S, 25.2510 E', Hakuto-R Mission 2 '60.4445 N, 4.588 W'; page states DE 421 mean Earth/polar axis frame, precision reflected by decimal places (0.001 deg ~ 30 m), footnote 'd' marks objects imaged by LROC, footnote 'f' says LROC shows no lander at the Luna 9 coordinates and footnote 'n' says the Luna 18 landing is unconfirmed.

authority: LROC Science Operations Team, Arizona State University (Wagner, Nelson, Plescia, Robinson, Speyerer, Mazarico)
title: Coordinates of Lunar Anthropogenic Targets (2016 LROC Coordinates of Robotic Spacecraft)
verified: Table of mean observed lat / lon (0-360 E) in the mean Earth/polar axis (ME) system with per-object uncertainty in metres, e.g. Surveyor 1 -2.4745 / 316.6602 (5.6 m), Luna 17 38.23764 / 324.99837 (0.5 m), Lunokhod 2 25.8323 / 30.9222 (7.5 m), Chang'e 3 44.1214 / 340.4883 (9.1 m), A13 SIVB -2.5550 / 332.1125, GRAIL-A 75.6088 / 333.4060, LADEE 11.8494 / 266.7506.

authority: NASA NSSDCA (Goddard Space Flight Center), curator D. R. Williams

authority: NASA History Program Office (A. A. Siddiqi, NASA SP-2018-4041)
title: Beyond Earth: A Chronicle of Deep Space Exploration, 1958-2016
verified: Luna 2 entry: launch '12 September 1959 / 06:39:42 UT'; 'impacted the surface of the Moon at 21:02:23 UT on 14 September 1959'; impact point 'approximately at 30° N / 0° longitude on the slope of the Autolycus crater'. Ranger IV entry: impact 'at 12:49:53 UT on 26 April 1962', 'Impact coordinates were 15.5° S / 229.3° E'.

title: 60 Years Ago: Luna 2 Makes Impact in Moon Race
verified: States 'On Sep. 13, Luna 2 became the first spacecraft to make contact with another celestial body', impacting 'between Mare Imbrium and Mare Serenitatis'; no time of day or coordinates given.

authority: NASA NSSDCA (Goddard Space Flight Center), curator D. R. Williams
